agree.reason: The memo is clear and well-structured, with a checkpoint and a plan for the ad sales lead, but the board members from advertising will see that it never says why ads have to end rather than run alongside membership, so they may not be moved.

honest.reason: It treats the $131,000-to-$84,000 fall as two years of decline ("about 20% a year") when it happened in a single year, and it claims one peer newsroom's result proves "the model works at our scale."

works_the_facts.reason: The figures are worked out well (150 members a month, 875 members needed, 55 a month required, about $52,000 in 2027), but the misread ad decline takes away the strongest true fact: ads fell 36% in one year.

right_comparison.reason: It frames doing nothing as a decline and projects it forward, but at 20% a year instead of the real 36%, so 2027 ads come out at $67,000 instead of about $54,000, and the year-one cash gap looks about $13,000 worse than it is.

qualification.reason: The checkpoint names a number (540 members), a date (30 June 2027) and a consequence (a revised plan within 30 days), and the board can check all three.

objections.reason: It covers early-joiner bias, cancellations, the cash gap and the ad lead's job, but it leaves out the objection the ad-background members are most likely to raise: why not keep the ads while membership grows?

fit.reason: It is a proper board memo with a clear decision request, about one page long, as the brief asked.
